front.title: Post-Quantum SecureChannel Profiles and Lifecycle Operations for IoT Deployments Using OPC UA

abstract.t:
This document addresses post-quantum SecureChannel migration for Internet of Things (IoT) deployments that already use OPC Unified Architecture (OPC UA), including fleets of capable controllers and industrial gateways with limited local user interfaces. It describes authorized application onboarding, credential and policy provisioning, bounded key use, renewal, failure recovery, quarantine, and retirement under existing device and application authorization.
A cryptographic protection profile for OPC UA Secure Conversation (UASC) over opc.tcp uses ML-KEM-768, ML-DSA, HKDF-SHA-256, and AES- 256-GCM. It specifies profile identifiers, nonce encoding, key derivation, authenticated encryption, identity binding, sequence and SecurityToken processing, per-key usage limits, and conformance requirements supporting those operations.
This individual submission proposes Standards Track publication and requests IOTOPS review of its IoT operational requirements. The appropriate venue for new protocol work requires separate determination. Permanent OPC UA SecurityPolicy and algorithm identifiers require coordination with the OPC Foundation; the private identifiers remain provisional and do not establish OPC Foundation conformance.
